The full rerun owed after each fork has no unit yet. Client versions on 2026-11-25 (critic query of web3_clientVersion on the networks.json endpoints): tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748, Geth/v1.8.2-4e1c8247-20261104 on BNB Chain, bor/f2a2d63e69f6/v2.11.1-private on Polygon, avalanchego/1.15.3, arc/v1 with no build named, 'hyperliquid evm Mainnet' with no build named, and reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb on Celo.

Polygon. Tag v2.11.2 of 0xPolygon/bor now exists (params/version.go at that tag sets VersionPatch = 2, fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com by the critic), and the endpoint still reports v2.11.1-private. core/vm/instructions.go, interpreter.go, analysis_legacy.go, jump_table.go, core/state/statedb.go, core/state/parallel_statedb.go, core/blockstm/executor.go, core/parallel_state_processor.go and params/config.go are byte identical between v2.11.1 and v2.11.2 (critic diff), so v2.11.2 changes nothing on the opcode path. v2.12.0-beta is different. It adds a widened keccak result cache for inputs from 1 to 8,192 bytes behind EnablePrecompileCache (core/vm/instructions.go lines 258-330, core/vm/interpreter.go lines 59-71), and the comment says the result caches that the import prefetcher and the parallel V2 workers share stay on when the flag is off. Cycle 12 read only the MULMOD memo of that beta (now core/vm/mulmod_memo.go, a per-EVM one-entry reciprocal memo). Nobody has read the widened keccak cache, the type keccakResultCache that it uses, or the shared result caches. The 58 byte position key and the pool id of the PoolManager would take the widened path.

Monad. theme-monad-harness-exact leaves four sites of the deployed PoolManager whose native register or stack arm no PoolManager scenario executed: CALLDATALOAD at pc 12232, MULMOD at pc 22378 (constant denominator 2^128), SAR at pc 15519 (BalanceDelta.amount0, src/types/BalanceDelta.sol:62-64) and SHL at pc 16642. It also shows that a planted fault at the other mul_mod2 site, pc 22639 (constant denominator 2^96), changes no result in 2,090 PoolManager scenarios and 2,007 mined transactions. For both mul_mod2 sites the micro programs are the only evidence that the remainder is right. The micro programs reach the same coarse shape, not the register allocation that the PoolManager's own block uses at that pc.

theme-revert-rollback-mined could not trace mined transactions on Arc (debug_traceTransaction answers -32601 on rpc.mainnet.arc.io, and arc.drpc.org answers 400), on Elysium (HTTP 401) or on Celo (no PoolManager logs in the last 4,000 blocks, and the archive endpoints tried did not trace). On these three networks the rollback of the unlock flag, deltas and synced reserves after a reverted frame has no producer evidence, only eth_call evidence.

The pyevm.py fault found in cycle 16 (a DELEGATECALL frame gets CALLVALUE 0, tools/opdiff/pyevm.py:205) was fixed only in the unit's own copy (pyevm_tx.py). The shared tool is unchanged, and no unit listed which earlier results ran pyevm.py over frames outside the PoolManager. The cycle 11 and 12 block-level removal simulators, the cycle 13 mined-branch replays and the cycle 16 whole-transaction reruns all used it. The PoolManager has no DELEGATECALL, so results limited to PoolManager frames stand. A replay that ran a router or multicall frame which reads msg.value under DELEGATECALL could have matched or failed for the wrong reason.

HyperEVM. The public replay clients pin ruint 1.15.0 (hyper-evm-sync) and 1.16.0 (nanoreth), as cycles 10 and 14 recorded. Both are inside RUSTSEC-2025-0137 (ruint::algorithms::div::reciprocal_mg10 relies on debug_assert and can read out of bounds in release builds for affected versions below 1.17.0; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rustsec/advisory-db/main/crates/ruint/RUSTSEC-2025-0137.md, fetched by the critic). The cycle 10 library reading discussed RUSTSEC-2026-0220 and two ruint issues, and does not mention this advisory for these two clients. The validator's own versions are still unknown (L-618).

op-stack-eth cleared F-133 for OP Mainnet, Base, Zora and World Chain from a reading of revm 42.0.0, which answers storage of created, destroyed and non-existent accounts without a database read. F-133 also names Celo, X Layer and reth-bsc. Their execution stacks pin older interpreters (celo-org/revm at revm-interpreter 35.0.1, X Layer revm-interpreter 37.0.3, reth-bsc revm-interpreter 35.0.1, as recorded in the cleared items of cycles 9, 11 and 12). Nobody has checked that those revm versions skip the database read in the same cases.

MegaETH. The stateless validator now builds and has validated 43,645 blocks. It ran only on blocks that hold a PoolManager log or a cycle 11 sampled transaction, and only up to block 32,766,000. A native-only settle or a clear emits no PoolManager log, so blocks that hold only those were not run. In --block-list mode the witness pre-state is not anchored to the parent root; only 45 blocks ran in anchored mode.

leads.question: In bor v2.12.0-beta, find the definition of keccakResultCache (used at core/vm/interpreter.go:62 and core/vm/instructions.go:313-330) and of the result caches that the import prefetcher and the parallel V2 workers share. Is the key the full input bytes copied out of EVM memory, or the slice returned by scope.Memory.GetPtr, or a fingerprint of the input? Can an entry written by a speculative execution that BlockSTM later aborts be read by another worker? Which bor release first ships this code, and does Polygon's validator configuration set EnablePrecompileCache?
leads.why: Every pool id (a keccak over the 160 byte PoolKey) and every position key (58 bytes, src/libraries/Position.sol) would go through this cache. A key that aliases memory or is a fingerprint lets one input return the hash of another. That would give a wrong storage slot for a pool, a position or a claim balance on a path that any account drives with chosen calldata. The 64 byte path copies its key into a [64]byte array (instructions.go:270-272); the widened path passes data straight to Load and Store.

leads.question: At the two mul_mod2 sites of the native PoolManager code (pc 22378, denominator 2^128, and pc 22639, denominator 2^96), take the exact register and stack arm that the PoolManager's own block uses in the instrumented asm log, and run micro programs on it where the correct remainder equals prod0, prod0 + 1 and prod0 - 1 and where prod1 is 1. Then answer by reading src/libraries/FullMath.sol:44-54: if this native remainder were wrong, could prod1 := sub(prod1, gt(remainder, prod0)) take prod1 from 1 to 0 and turn the result into an amount below 2^160 that src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:68 and :90 and the casts of Pool.sol accept? Name the caller of each site (which SqrtPriceMath or Pool function passes Q96 or Q128) and whether an ordinary swap or modifyLiquidity reaches it with prod1 equal to 1.
leads.why: theme-monad-harness-exact shows that a planted fault at pc 22639 changes no result in 2,090 scenarios and 2,007 mined transactions. The PoolManager-level checks cannot see that site, and validators run compiled code that no RPC executes (F-130). A wrong borrow at the prod1 == 1 edge turns an overflow revert into an accepted small amount, which lets a caller pay about 2^160 less than owed. That would be a siphon by any account, so the compiled arm at that exact pc needs evidence of its own.

leads.question: Build PoolManager scenarios that reach the native SAR at pc 15519 (BalanceDelta.amount0, sar(128, delta), src/types/BalanceDelta.sol:62-64) and the SHL at pc 16642 through the register or stack-slot arm the PoolManager block uses, with deltas whose amount0 is -1, -2^127, 2^127 - 1 and 0 and whose amount1 has the top bit set. Run them interpreted and native in the cycle 16 harness.
leads.why: amount0 decides whether the caller owes or is owed currency0 in _accountPoolBalanceDelta. A sign error in one compiled arm would credit instead of debit. It is the only listed unexecuted arm that sits on the settlement path, and its coarse shape is covered only by 56 micro programs outside the PoolManager block.

leads.question: Run the cycle 16 offsets.py vectors (cycles/016/arbitrum-family.work: CALLDATALOAD, CALLDATACOPY, RETURNDATACOPY, MCOPY, CODECOPY and KECCAK256 with offsets from 2^31 to 2^256-1, zero lengths at large offsets, and return data copies whose offset plus length overflows) on the 18 networks where they were not run. Do the Go based clients (bor, BSC geth, avalanchego coreth, Celo op-geth backend) and the Monad interpreter give the Arbitrum result?
leads.why: These shapes meet the hook return copy and revert bubbling (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-160, src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol) and the ABI decoding of hookData and unlock data. They were aimed at a Go slice-index fault class (issues 79874 and 80517) that applies to any Go toolchain, not only the one Elysium uses, and were run only on the three Nitro chains.

leads.question: Patch tools/opdiff/pyevm.py:205 to pass the caller frame's value into DELEGATECALL, then list every earlier result that ran pyevm.py over a frame other than the PoolManager (block-level removal simulators of cycles 11 and 12, mined-branch replays of cycle 13, whole-transaction reruns of cycle 16). Rerun the ones whose transactions contain a DELEGATECALL frame that reads CALLVALUE. Does any matched or unmatched outcome change?
leads.why: The reference interpreter is the oracle for producer evidence on Monad, MegaETH and HyperEVM. A known fault in it means some of those matches may rest on a wrong model, and the review has not said which ones.

leads.question: When Tempo publishes the release that carries T15 (main on 2026-11-25 still pins evm2 rev 35aa3280 and ruint 1.21.1 in Cargo.lock, fetched by the critic), diff its Cargo.lock for ruint, evm2 and alloy-primitives. Read every changed handler of MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, the shifts, SIGNEXTEND, BYTE, the jump destination scan and TLOAD and TSTORE. Rerun battery.py, targeted.py and the 8,908 mulDiv vectors of the ruint 1.21.0 fault against a node of that release before activation, using a simulated block time after the fork as cycle 7 did for T14.
leads.why: Tempo is the one network with a single client on the rewritten ruint paths. The October 2026 MULMOD fault reached a release in three days. A new arithmetic fault there would reach every swap and would be usable by any account, with no second client to stop the block.

leads.question: For celo-reth (revm-interpreter 35.0.1 from celo-org/revm), X Layer reth v0.0.7 (revm-interpreter 37.0.3) and reth-bsc, does State::storage or its equivalent answer storage of an account created, not existing or destroyed in the block without a database read, as op-stack-eth read for revm 42.0.0? Is there any default path that puts a storage word of a codeless address into the reth execution cache?

leads.question: F-132 is recorded as confirmed (low), and OPCODES.md says it hangs on one unproven link: a read that puts a storage word of a codeless address into the cache first. op-stack-eth now shows that no default path makes that read on Base's revm. Does a block builder with the cache flag on take any path that the default path does not, so that F-132 stays, or should F-132 be downgraded to match F-133?
leads.why: The ledger holds a confirmed finding and a cleared item that rest on opposite answers to the same link.

leads.question: In ruint 1.15.0 and 1.16.0, which functions call algorithms::div::reciprocal_mg10, and is every caller's divisor normalised (top bit set) before the call on the paths revm 19.2.0 and the nanoreth revm 29.0.1 fork use for DIV, MOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD and SDIV? Check src/algorithms/div of both tags and the revm interpreter call sites.
leads.why: RUSTSEC-2025-0137 is unsound in release builds for these versions and is the only open arithmetic advisory against the public HyperEVM replay clients. They are the only re-execution of the closed validator's blocks. If an input reaches it unnormalised, the archive client could disagree with the validator on a mulDiv, or the validator itself could compute wrongly if it pins the same version.

leads.question: Run the built MegaETH stateless validator in chain-following mode from the PoolManager deployment block to the head, including blocks with PoolManager transactions that emit no PoolManager log (native settle, clear, sync only). Find such blocks from the callTracer of transactions to the PoolManager address or from eth_getBlockReceipts filtered by 'to'. Report any block that fails.
leads.why: This closes the coverage left by the --block-list run (blocks with logs only, up to 32,766,000, pre-state anchored on 45 blocks only). It is the one public check of the closed MegaETH producer's full post-state.

leads.question: Rerun pmdiff 1, 2 and 6 with the PoolManager bytecode placed at the real PoolManager address of each network (code and storage left as on chain, only the driver injected by state override), not at the fresh override address. Does any network answer differently at its real address?
leads.why: Every script comparison so far ran the bytecode at a fresh address with its immutable rewritten. Rules that a node keys on an address, such as Arc's value-call frame hook, Avalanche's slot fold on existing storage, Tempo's TIP-403 policies, MegaETH's per-account gas accounting and any JIT or compile decision keyed by address or hotness, never applied to those runs.

leads.question: Extend the bracketed-credits table to permissionless relays outside the canonical bridges and CCTP. LayerZero executor lzReceive for OFT tokens such as USDT0, Wormhole Token Bridge completeTransfer for transfers without payload, Hyperlane process, and Axelar execute. For each, can any account execute a verified message whose recipient is the PoolManager inside its own transaction, and has any such message named a PoolManager?
leads.why: This is the same low hazard class as the CCTP finding and F-135, and it completes the class in one pass. Record it in one line per relay unless a relay pays a recipient that its owner did not choose.

leads.question: Which Monad release do mainnet validators run? The official docs pin 0.16.5 for mainnet and the three public RPC endpoints answer Monad/0.16.7. Settle it from monad-bft block headers or the validator version field if one is published. If it cannot be settled, say that both versions are covered by the cycle 16 harness and close the lead.
leads.why: The N-3 header check makes RPC nodes agree with the quorum on mined blocks. Input no mined block has used is covered only by the harness, and the harness covers both versions, so this matters only if validators run a third version.

leads.question: mega-evm v1.7.3 rewrites a CREATE frame (and a SELFDESTRUCT whose usage was recorded before it halted) to Revert after revm has committed it (crates/mega-evm/src/limit/limit.rs:801-856). Does any other network's client report a frame as failed while keeping its writes? Candidates are Arc's value-call frame hook (F-125), the Tempo TIP-20 policy checks, Monad's reserve balance check at depth zero and HyperEVM's CoreWriter. For each, say whether the failure is decided before the callee runs or after it has written state.
leads.why: The PoolManager reverts whenever a callee fails, and a parent revert rolls back a committed child, so the MegaETH rule cannot reach pool funds. The same reasoning needs to be stated for each network that has a frame hook of its own, so the clearance does not rest on MegaETH alone.
